pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/analyze/AnalyzeApi.ts:181 This context is client-side intake and run-delivery state that POSTs a form to the server analysis route. A recursive search of app/features/tools/analyze for systemPrompt, buildPrompt, assemblePrompt and max_tokens found nothing; the only 'prompt' hits are the English words 'promptly' and 'prompt poll' (AnalyzeApi.ts:224, :324). It assembles no model prompt.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/companion-turn.ts:124 transcriptWindow keeps the newest 12 eligible turns and drops older ones with no count or notice; companion_cli.py then renders the remainder under 'THIS CONVERSATION SO FAR', so in a long thread the model takes a partial history to be the whole conversation.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/companion-turn.ts:124 The bottom rung is silence, not a notice. Only {role, content} is shipped, with no dropped-turn count. The grounding summary also cuts the board to the busiest 5 roles (line 179, `.slice(0, TOP_ROLES)`) with no 'N more roles' line, inside a block the prompt labels 'the only facts you may state as facts'.

app/_lib/companion-turn.ts:15 The durable record lives in the store and the prompt is rebuilt every turn, which is the projection regime. Yet history is a fixed recent window with no coarser tier reaching the start of a thread the code itself calls 'a year of conversations' (line 273). Episodic recall is a memory store, not a projection of the record.

app/_lib/companion-run.ts:33 The Node side ships one typed turn.json and no prompt prose. One assembler (companion_cli._system_prompt and _build_prompt) owns the layers: constitution → identity → contracts → language, then grounding → recall → transcript → fenced operator message.

app/_lib/companion-run.ts:262 The action addendum in the prompt and the dispatch validator are both derived from the COMPANION_ACTIONS registry (companion-actions.ts:16). Proposals are re-validated on the Node side, and an empty catalog teaches the model nothing.

app/_lib/companion-run.ts:87 The CLI never queries kp, so the board state cannot be reached any other way. It is injected as standing grounding from one function, companionGrounding, which treats it as a floor.
